William Morgan King Jr. (born June 22, 1946) is an American-born Canadian pianist, composer, record producer, musical director, broadcaster, photographer, and festival curator. He is best known for serving as musical director for artists such as Janis Joplin, Linda Ronstadt, and The Pointer Sisters, founding Toronto’s Beaches International Jazz Festival, and leading programming at the Redwood Theatre.
Early life
King was born in Jeffersonville, Indiana. He studied classical piano and was awarded scholarships to attend the Oscar Peterson Advanced School of Contemporary Music in Toronto and Berklee College of Music in Boston.
Career
Musical direction and performance
By 1968, King had relocated from Greenwich Village to Los Angeles to become Linda Ronstadt’s music director and pianist. A year later, he joined Janis Joplin’s band in the same capacity. He subsequently toured as musical director for Martha Reeves and The Pointer Sisters.
Throughout his career, King has performed with artists such as Chaka Khan, Jackie Richardson, Liberty Silver, and Sophie Milman. He has led bands including the Saturday Nite Fish Fry, the Bill King Trio, and Rhythm Express.
Recording and labels
King released his debut album Goodbye Superdad in 1969 on Capitol Records, followed by Dixie Peach in 1970. In 1984, he founded the Night Passage label, and in 1992 co-founded Radioland Records with Greg Sutherland.
His discography includes:
* Magnolia Nights (1993)
* Mondo Jumbo (2007)
* Night Passage (2010)
* The Color of Heaven (2019)
Broadcasting and journalism
In the 1980s, King began a radio career with Q107, then created and hosted The Jazz Report on CIUT-FM, which evolved into a national jazz radio network (1989–1991). He later hosted Jazz Preview on JAZZ.FM91 for over four years, and currently co-hosts The Bill & Jesse King Show on CIUT alongside his son Jesse King (a.k.a. Dubmatix).
King also co-founded The Jazz Report magazine in 1987 and served as its editor-in-chief.
Executive director, Redwood Theatre
In 2023, King was appointed Executive Director of the Redwood Theatre, a historic 1914 vaudeville venue in Toronto. Under his leadership, the venue expanded its programming to include jazz concerts, film screenings, variety shows, and community arts events.
Festival leadership
King co-founded the Beaches International Jazz Festival in 1988 and has served as its artistic director since its inception. The festival has grown into one of Canada’s largest free music events, presenting hundreds of acts annually across multiple stages in Toronto.
Photography
King is an award-winning street and performance photographer. His work has appeared in publications such as DownBeat, The Globe and Mail, and Toronto Star, and has been exhibited at the Contact Photography Festival.
Awards and recognition
* Juno Award nominee – Best Jazz Recording for Avenue B (1985)
* National Jazz Award: Producer of the Year (2003, 2004)
* National Jazz Award: Jazz Photographer of the Year (2007)
